topics.caution: Vishnu's line that only a 'mahatyagi purush's willingly-given bones' can kill Vritra is the plot's turning device, but the explanation could slide into a literal theology statement about what a devotee owes a god, or into 'this is how Hindus believe weapons are made'.
topics.guidance: Explain it as the story's own logic that sets up the search for Dadhichi — a storytelling device that makes the ત્યાગ possible — not as a factual or devotional claim about how the world works; keep the tatsama words (અસ્થિ, મહાત્યાગી) glossed at the point of use rather than reworded.

topics.caution: This topic carries Dadhichi's actual death — his joy at giving up his body, 'શાંતિ ! શાંતિ ! શાંતિ !', and the ripe-fruit/feather imagery for his dying. The explanation or real_life_example could turn this into a lesson that giving up one's own life or body is something a child should aspire to literally, or could dwell on the physical death in a way that unsettles a std-8 child, or could be read as a devotional instruction about how to die well.
topics.guidance: Teach this as the story's ચોટ — Dadhichi's willing, joyful ત્યાગ for the good of the three worlds ('ત્રણ લોકમાં સૌ કોઈનું કલ્યાણ હો') — and name the author's craft in the ripe-fruit/feather comparison as a peaceful, literary way of showing his passing, never as an instruction. Keep real_life_example anchored in a child's own world of generosity and helping others (e.g. donating blood, sharing what one has, helping a neighbour in trouble) rather than in death or self-sacrifice itself; the recall answer for this topic must stay text-grounded in what Dadhichi says and does, not extend into 'a person should also be ready to die for others'.

chapter_level.guidance: The whole chapter is a પૌરાણિક કથા built around ભગવાન વિષ્ણુ, ઇંદ્ર and the sage દધીચિ. Teach it as literature with a living tradition behind it — its ભાવ (the value of selfless ત્યાગ) and its craft (the ripe-fruit imagery, the ascent of gods and gandharvas) — never as theology, never as comparative religion, and never with any line that verifies or debunks the events against science or history. This binds `explanation`, `summary`, `detailed_summary`, `real_life_example` and every recall/exercise answer across all nine topics.

The chapter's conflict (devas versus Vritra) exists only to set up Dadhichi's ત્યાગ, not the other way round. Keep the teaching centred on courage and generosity — the willingness to give for the good of others — and never on the violence of the demon's death or on the killing itself as a triumph to dwell on; the discussion-box theme itself is 'ત્યાગનો આનંદ / ત્યાગનો મહિમા', and the teaching should follow that same centre of gravity.
